## What's new

**More ways in.** Until now DB Mastermind was built for one team. This release is for everyone: it starts from what you already have.

- **Connections from your project.** Drop a `.env`, a docker-compose file or a project folder on the window (or *Import connections → From a project folder…*): the databases it names become connections, with their passwords saved encrypted. `DATABASE_URL`, the `DB_*` / `PG*` / `MYSQL_*` sets, compose services with their published ports and a Prisma datasource are read.
- **Hosted databases by name.** Paste a connection string from Supabase, Neon, Timescale, Amazon RDS or Aurora, Azure Database, Azure SQL or Google Cloud SQL: the form says which service it is and turns TLS on. CockroachDB has its own entry in the list of databases.
- **Models from other tools.** Open a Mermaid `erDiagram`, a drawDB file, a MySQL Workbench `.mwb` or a Prisma schema as a model (*Open a model*, the model's Import, or drop the file). Table positions, colors and notes come along; the file you open is never changed. What could not be taken is counted in a notice, never dropped silently.
- **Code from a model or a live database.** *Export → Code* in any diagram writes a Prisma schema, a Drizzle schema, SQLAlchemy models or TypeScript types; `dbm export` does the same from the command line. Each format is checked in CI by its own tool: Prisma, the TypeScript compiler and SQLAlchemy.
- **`dbmastermind-mcp` as a package of its own.** The MCP server and the `dbm` command line run without the desktop app. Publishing to npm and the MCP registry is prepared and follows shortly; until then the server comes with the desktop app (*Settings → MCP server*) or is built from the repository (`npm run build -w packages/mcp`).

**Easier at first sight.** A review of the whole app as a stranger meets it, and of the small things daily use had shown.

- **Tabs:** the **+** for a new tab is always in view, also with many tabs and with no connection selected. The strip fades only on a side that hides tabs, the selected tab always stays in view, a reopened tab returns to its place, and ⇧⌘] / ⇧⌘[ (Ctrl+PageDown / PageUp) switch tabs. A tab's menu has **Close tabs to the left** and **Close tabs to the right**. The strip can be walked with the keyboard, and open tabs are in the command palette.
- **Scroll or shrink:** *Settings → Appearance → When tabs don't fit* chooses between scrolling the strip (as before) and narrowing the tabs; the selected tab always keeps its full width.
- **The demo database opens on a table with data**, not on an empty editor, and on a fresh start page it is a button of its own next to *New connection*.
- **Toolbars keep their labels** whenever they fit; they give way to icons only when the bar would overflow.
- **Errors say what happened and what to do:** "Nothing is listening on host:port", "No host named …", a rejected password, a missing database, an AI key the provider didn't accept; the server's own words stay below.
- **AI is ready as soon as a provider has its key:** no extra "Use this provider" click. *Fix with AI*, *Explain with AI* and *Design with AI* open the setup when no provider is set up yet, and each starts its own chat.
- **Unsaved changes in a table show on its tab**, and closing, refreshing, disconnecting or quitting asks *Save / Discard / Cancel*.
- **In the SQL editor** Enter and Tab accept the highlighted suggestion the moment the list opens.
- Notices no longer cover a dialog's buttons; the model's main button reads *Compare with database* in full; the selection's average is rounded as the column is; the Teal accent and the green terminal look pass contrast checks.

**Security: the read-only guard, rebuilt.** SQL that nobody confirmed (from the AI assistant and from agents over MCP) and everything on a read-only connection runs behind a guard. An independent review of this release found that crafted comments and quoting could get a write past it in every version so far, on PostgreSQL and SQL Server, and a file written on a MySQL server. Nobody is known to have been affected; update if agents or an assistant work with databases that matter.

- The guard no longer depends on how the app reads the SQL. The database decides: PostgreSQL gets one statement per message and its transaction status is checked after each; SQL Server plans every batch first and only reading statements pass; the other engines get the strictest mode each offers. Only statements that start as a read are let through at all.
- Every read-only connection now uses the same guard, on every engine, and so do raw conditions typed into a table's filter.
- It is tested against the real servers with more than a thousand generated attacks per engine, in CI.
- One limit to know: on MySQL and MariaDB, writing a server file (`INTO OUTFILE`) can't be forbidden by the server per statement; the app refuses it, and a login without the `FILE` privilege closes it for good.
- Two of the AI's tools, the one that samples a table and the one that explains a query, did not go through the guard on connections that allow writing. Every tool now reaches the database through one narrow, guarded view and nothing else.
- DuckDB: SQL nobody confirmed reads the database file and the files you opened in the app with *Query a file* (or dropped on it); for `dbmastermind-mcp` and `dbm` name them with `--allow-files`.

**AI permissions hold from the first moment to the last.**

- They are checked again for every tool call, every approval and every write: turning AI off for a connection, or lowering it to *Schema only*, applies to a chat that is already running and to an agent that is already connected.
- AI turned off by your organization or team folder follows the server: a duplicate of the connection, another database on it or an imported copy is off too.
- *Schema only* means no value from a row reaches the AI: query plans come without running the query, and errors that would quote a value are shortened.
- The token of the app's MCP endpoint is stored encrypted like passwords and API keys (yours keeps its value).

**Values written into SQL scripts.** *Export as SQL*, *Copy as SQL INSERT* and the script that syncs two tables wrote every value with one database's rules. On MySQL and MariaDB a text with a backslash came out wrong, and a crafted value in a table could end its string and continue as SQL in the script. Values are now written by the rules of the database the script is for, checked by loading 300 awkward values through each kind of script on eight engines.

**Smaller, from the same reviews.** Trino: credentials are sent only to the server of the connection, never to an address its answer names. A knowledge base can't be led out of its folder by a link inside it. Names of roles, sequences and constraints reach SQL as parameters or quoted.

**Careful with files from strangers.** A model somebody mailed you or a repository you cloned is untrusted input.

- Size limits before anything is read, zip archives inflated only as far as needed, no links followed out of a project folder, and nothing from a file is ever run.
- Text from a model can't escape into the code or the SQL scripts that are generated from it: names and comments are written as the target language requires, and every expression from a model is re-written in the target database's plainest form before it goes into a script; what can't be read safely is left out and listed as a warning. Thousands of hostile models are part of the tests.
- The app's main process reads a file only when you handed it over: a dialog, a drop on the window, or the command line.

**Also fixed**

- MySQL: a model from a SQL script, from MySQL Workbench and the live database now compare as the same (UNSIGNED is kept; BOOLEAN and `tinyint(1)` are one type; the index MySQL makes for a foreign key is no difference).
- DBML written by other tools reads the same as in dbdiagram.io (one-line blocks, settings over several lines, `Ref` blocks); an unclosed bracket is an error on its line instead of a model that silently loses tables.
- SQL scripts: a column named `key` or `index` is a column; MySQL's versioned comments, FULLTEXT and SPATIAL indexes are read.
- SQL Server connection URLs with a user and password (`sqlserver://user:password@host:1433;databaseName=…`) and `encrypt` / `trustServerCertificate` in every form.
- ClickHouse: a query that fails after it started sending rows shows its error instead of rows.
- PostgreSQL `bit(n)` is exported as a bit string, not as a boolean.
- Linux: the `.deb` runs inside Chromium's sandbox; the AppImage does where the system allows it and says so on start where it doesn't.

The website is new: [dbmastermind.app](https://dbmastermind.app), with a [getting started guide](https://dbmastermind.app/guide.html).

Updates itself on Windows (installer), macOS and Linux (AppImage). The [Microsoft Store](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9p0grd7bz4nf) version updates through the Store.

## Download

| | |
|---|---|
| Windows, signed by Microsoft | [Microsoft Store](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9p0grd7bz4nf) |
| Windows, no installation | `DB-Mastermind-1.5.0-win-x64-portable.zip`: unzip and run `DB Mastermind.exe` |
| Windows installer (no admin, updates itself) | `DB-Mastermind-1.5.0-win-x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows for IT (per machine) | `DB-Mastermind-1.5.0-win-x64.msi` |
| Windows via Scoop | `scoop install https://github.com/eLh0m3r0/db-mastermind/releases/latest/download/db-mastermind.json` |
| macOS | `…-mac-arm64.dmg` (Apple Silicon) / `…-mac-x64.dmg` (Intel), or `brew tap elh0m3r0/db-mastermind https://github.com/eLh0m3r0/db-mastermind && brew install --cask db-mastermind`. First launch: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway (the app is not notarized yet) |
| Linux | `DB-Mastermind-linux-x86_64.AppImage` (updates itself; needs FUSE 2, `libfuse2t64` on Ubuntu 24.04) or `.deb` |
| MCP server and command line | inside the desktop app (*Settings → MCP server*); the npm package follows |
